static UC(closure)[source]¶

Function to get universal correction (UC) based on the closure used for RISM calculation. function returns a dictionary containing both the FEP and experimental correction constants ‘A’ and ‘B’ in the equation: delta G^{solv} = mu^{ex}+’A’*V_m+’B’; where V_m is partial molar volume from the free energy universal correction proposed by: David S Palmer, Andrey I Frolov, Ekaterina L Ratkova and Maxim V Fedorov http://dx.doi.org/10.1088/0953-8984/22/49/492101 :param

free_energy(conv='kj/mol', fit_value='EXP')[source]¶

Return the free energy of the most recent calculation according to the 3DRISM object ==================== fit_value: string, energy value to return options: EXP : experimental fitting FEP : free energy of pertubation fitting ==================== conv: sting expression default output unit is in !!!! in KJ/mol !!!! can specify what units you want to convert to by specifying the expression. Function will return the value based on original unit convversion e.g “kcal” resolves to taking original free energy value in Kj/mol and multipying it by (1/Kj)*(2kcal)*1mol to convert to kcal ———– keyword Options: ———– kcal, mol , kj, j , joule ——— all other standard math symbols allowed ———–

delta G^{solv} = mu^{ex}+’A’*V_m+’B’, where V_m is partial molar volume

Parameters:

  • conv (str)

  • fit_value (str)

placement(num_waters_to_place, atom_to_select='O', radius=1.9269073728633292, filename=False, grid_spacing=None, write_pdb=False, outname='out.pdb', weight=None)[source]¶

function places an atom at the (grid) location with the highest density, then removes the density surrounding the region according to a probe and continues the search until all atoms are placed. kind of like placevent. or Ambers/openeye ‘blob’ method, but those are so boring and you can specify the number of atoms you want to place. This method is super simple and also naive which means it works.

Parameters:

  • num_waters_to_place (int) – number of waters to place

  • atom_to_select – str ( O: oxygen, H: hydrogen, MG: magnesium) int (column of txt file to select)

  • radius (float) – distance around selected point to omit from remaining placement in Angstrom

  • filename (bool)

  • write_pdb (bool)

  • outname (str)

  • weight (bool)

ideal_radius = ((10**3)/(4/3)/(np.pi)/33.3679)**(1/3) based on number density of water :param filename: txt file containing density, format is: (columns) x,y,z val_1 (oxygen) val_2 (hydrogen) val_3 (your mixture) :param grid_spacing: conversion from array indices to angstrom, units of 1/A, the program automatically converts for you but you can override if need be :param outname: string for pdb file :param write_pdb: kind of uh, self explanitory, need to update bc its useless, if you specify outname then write_pdb is set to true :param weight: numpy array with the same dimensions as your 3DRISM calc. or the filename that you inserted. they is just multiplied together…

rism(step=500, resolution=1, values_to_save='all', *args)[source]¶

Sets the steps and resolution of the calculation. Will automatically set number of grids based on the box dimensions acquired from cls.solute()

Parameters:

  • step (int) – int(), Number of SCF steps to perform

  • resolution (float) – grid resolution of box (will override if previously set)

  • values_to_save (str) – values to save to the dump file; options below: * all : reports all of the below * command : save the exact command that was run when the file was produced * guv : g(r) foreach grid point * ld : smoothed g(r) i.e. g(r) convolved with kernel * coul : coulombic potential at each grid * excess : mu^ex at each grid

  • *args –

    endless possibilities here

select_grid(input_string='guv', coord_array=None)[source]¶

select values in array based on the selection input string so far selection string is limited to selection of grid-values around single residue names only: i.e. around 4 resname LYS But we reccommend using the coordinate array input for more in-depth selections selection string can include the following key-words any output value from 3DRISM, i.e ‘guv’, ‘uuv’ or ‘coul’ etc. etc. around ‘distance’. select grid values around coordinates within specified distance (in Angstrom)

  • get :: get the exact grid value on the input coordinates (i.e. resname or coord_array)

  • resname :: any 3-letter cannonical residue name, upper or lower case

  • ‘laplace’ or ‘laplacian’ or ‘lap’ or ‘grad’ or ‘gradient’ or ‘del’ :: return laplacian of the whole grid

this selection can be used in tandem with ‘around’ and ‘get’ but will always return the laplacian of the original unmasked grid, and NOT the laplacian of the selection region. * ‘convolve’ or ‘log’ or ‘laplacian of gaussian’ :: return the grid convolved with a laplacian of gaussian (LoG) filter. Same specification as above, usse sigma stdev. for gaussian kernel in the LoG filter

example selection ` cls.select_grid('LoG of guv with sigma 3 around 4 resname MOL') ` creates laplacian of gaussian of the g(r) grid with a gaussian std. of 3, then selects the region around 4 A of all atoms in the residue named ‘MOL’

:param : :type : param input_string: value to select and extract :param : :type : param coord_array: N x 3 array of positons to select around

Parameters:

input_string (str)

class episol.fileutils.amber_inp(filename=None, outname=None, debug=False)[source]¶

Bases: dict

Manipulate an amber[1] .inp file for 1DRISM calculations. this function reads in an amber .inp file for 1DRISM calculations as a dictionary. and allows the user to change parameters. This is useful as amber 1DRISM will create a .sav file after each run and as long as you dont change grid spacing or length. it will reuse the previous run results (.sav). allowing for quick convergence.

Example usage: ``` temps = [i for i in range(100,1000,100)] density = [10,20,… etc] input_1drism = amber_inp(“molecule.inp”) # then loop through thermo values and redo 1DRISM for dens,temp in zip(density,temps):

input_1drism.temp = temp input_1drism.desnity = dens input_1drism.write() # overwrites existing file os.system(“rism1d molecule”) … do something … etc.

```

References

[1] AmberTools D.A. Case, H.M. Aktulga, K. Belfon, D.S. Cerutti, G.A. Cisneros, V.W.D. Cruz eiro, N. Forouzesh, T.J. Giese, A.W. Götz, H. Gohlke, S. Izadi, K. Kasavajhala, M.C. Kaymak, E. King, T. episol.fileutils.try_getpass()[source]¶

getpass.getuser() will fail when using a docker container where the PID and UID is not copied into the container. You can combat this yourself when pulling an image. BUT you dont have a choice if you are using someone elses (your uni or job) scheduling software. As it pulls it for you, and they probably dont transfer your UID.
